pr_title: process more TLS frames at one when available
pr_body:
This is fragment of original #49743
This change will process more frames if already read from transport returning bigger chunks of data to caller. 
Aside from the big loop change this adds more spanification and tracing for EOF as we may reach it while already decrypted some data.

AuxRecord tests are removed as they depend on particular read side. 

fixes #49000

I did another pass towards direction we discussed @geoffkizer. 
While this is not 100% complete it would be great if you can take another look and provide feedback. 
To make that more manageable I moved all the IO to `getFullFrameIfNeed()` and I also added `haveFullTlsFrame()` helper function to make it more obvious.

This is definitely a step in the right direction, but I think we can still reorganize some of the logic in ReadAsyncInternal to make it simpler and easier to follow.

Here's how I would organize the logic:

(1) Copy already-decrypted data (if any). If this fills the user buffer, we are done.
(2) Process as many buffered frames as we have, by decrypting them and then copying the decrypted data into the user buffer. If we fill the user buffer, we are done.
(3) If we provided any data to the user, we are done -- no more buffered data to process.
(4) Check for EOF previously read. If so, we are done, return 0 bytes.
(5) Do zero-byte read if necessary
(6) Read into buffer, repeating until we have a full frame or get EOF. If valid EOF (i.e. no partial frame), set EOF and return 0 bytes; for partial frame and EOF, throw.
(7) Repeat step 2, i.e. decrypt and copy until user buffer is full or we run out of buffered data.

Since step (2) and (7) are the same, I would factor them out into something like a "DecryptBufferedFrames" method.

I ignored renegotiation here but I think it's straightforward to add it in...

Thoughts?

I moved decrypt logic to separate function and the main loop now looks pretty simple.
